title: Concept art: Enochian realm key art (nephilim battle, element bricks)
description:
## Subject

Hero key art for the Enochian re-theme of this breakout clone: realm I, "The Watchers'
Camp" (element earth). One 16:9 painterly frame showing the whole gameplay fiction at
once — the titan-brick ranks, the ship-paddle, and the ball of divine light mid-arc.

## Use in game

Establishes the canonical look for all five realms and every subsequent asset. Used as
the title/menu backdrop, the realm-I loading plate, and the reference every later
concept is judged against. The mechanic it must make legible: bricks are ranks of
nephilim titans floating in formation; the paddle is an ancient warship; clearing the
last brick translocates the ship to the next realm, where the battle is already raging.

Because it doubles as the style proof, it has to survive being viewed at 1x and at
thumbnail size in a contact sheet.

## Variants

4 variations in round 1 on `google/gemini-2.5-flash-image`, all from one prompt. If a
variant is picked, one refinement round on `google/gemini-3-pro-image` with the pick
passed as `--ref` for fidelity. Expect 4 more frames there.

Successor pieces in the same lane, filed separately once this look is locked:
element brick sheet (4 distinct silhouettes), the translocation beat (realm I → II),
and the ship design at gameplay scale.

## Frames

Static. No animation frames in this issue. The ball's arc is painted as a single
trajectory streak, not a sprite sequence.

## References

`art/style.md` is binding — palette, prompt preamble, Do/Don't all come from it.

Composition and register anchors, in priority order:
- `art/enoch_concept/ref_crop_watchers.png` — primary. Muted teal-sage colossus over an
  umber valley, one tiny mortal for scale. Closest to the intended register.
- `art/enoch_concept/nephilim-600nw-2505030389.png` — bone-cloud scale, gold cloud-break.
- `art/enoch_concept/360_F_988089084_sFoLE85aCf9sTdaMsogUiwpajtCuxAQe.png` — fire realm,
  ember colossus (reserve for realm IV).
- `art/enoch_concept/ai-generated-8464195_640.png` — encampment with giants looming,
  held for the translocation piece.

`ref_crop_axe.png` is a costume/material study for the titans, not a composition anchor.

All references are licensed stock previews: private mood only, never shipped or
published. The generated art derives from them and must not reproduce any watermark,
agency footer, or logo badge.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] 16:9 widescreen frame, minimum 1920x1080, saved as PNG
- [ ] no text, lettering, sigils, logos, watermarks, borders, signatures or UI overlays anywhere in the image
- [ ] matches the art/style.md palette: muted earthen frame with a single divine gold source; no neon, no chromatic bloom, no glossy specular
- [ ] no violet or magenta (reserved for realm V)
- [ ] brick ranks read as clearly separable rectangular blocks, not organic blobs, and are countable as rows at 1x
- [ ] the four element hues stay distinguishable at 1x if element variants appear
- [ ] the warship is present, small, bottom-centre, and legible as the paddle at gameplay scale
- [ ] the ball of light and its arc into the titan ranks are visible as one trajectory
- [ ] something deliberately small is in frame for scale, placed low
- [ ] clean dark space in both top corners for HUD overlay
- [ ] survives thumbnail viewing in the contact sheet without losing the read
- [ ] no reference watermark or badge reproduced from any source image
- [ ] picked variant recorded via `artgen pick`, prompt copied to art/enoch_concept/prompts/, round dir has meta.json
close_reason: Superseded by the Steelbreak theme (user decision 2026-09-27); see sim-rdl.5

title: Stop tracking trunk build output (dist/) in git
description: dist/ (trunk build output: index.html, sim-<hash>.js, sim-<hash>_bg.wasm) is committed to the repo but not in .gitignore (which only has /target). Every local `trunk build` - a required check in .claude/workflow.yaml - dirties the tree with deleted/new hashed files, which contributors must restore by hand before committing. Found while working on sim-v0i.1. Decide whether Pages deploy relies on the committed dist/ (CI builds it itself?) and, if not, git rm -r --cached dist and add /dist to .gitignore.

comments.author: frede
comments.text: [pm] Resolved open question: .github/workflows/build.yml runs 'trunk build --release' itself and uploads that dist/ to Pages, so the committed dist/ is unused. Approach: git rm -r --cached dist, add /dist to .gitignore. AC: dist/ untracked; 'trunk build' leaves git status clean; CI native+web jobs and Pages deploy still green.

title: Make Lua scripting (bevy_mod_scripting/lua54) native-only so the wasm build compiles
description:
## Problem
bevy_mod_scripting 0.21 with the `lua54` feature is currently an unconditional dependency in Cargo.toml. `lua54` builds mlua's bundled Lua C sources, which do not compile for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, so `trunk build` (the primary distribution target) and the CI `web` job / GitHub Pages deploy fail.

## Approach
Same pattern as the existing avian2d/getrandom target gating (no gameplay changes):
1. Cargo.toml: move `bevy_mod_scripting = { version = "0.21.0", features = ["lua54"] }` out of `[dependencies]` into `[target.'cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))'.dependencies]`.
2. src/main.rs: gate `mod script_manager;` and `.add_plugins(script_manager::ScriptPlugin)` with `#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]` (or give ScriptPlugin a no-op wasm impl so main.rs stays ungated).
3. Optional: also put it behind a Cargo feature (e.g. `scripting`, default-on) so native builds can opt out with `--no-default-features`. Note that a feature alone isn't enough: trunk would still enable it for wasm unless the dependency is also target-gated.

## Acceptance criteria
- `cargo build` (native) still includes and runs ScriptPlugin/BMSPlugin.
- `trunk build --release` succeeds and the game runs in the browser without scripting.
- CI `native` and `web` jobs are green on master, and the Pages deploy succeeds (https://frederickbrock.github.io/breakout/).
- CLAUDE.md "wasm enablement" note updated to mention scripting is native-only.

title: Gameplay feel: mouse control, anchored serve, power-up bricks, Steelbreak look
description:
## Problem / goal
Make the game feel like a real Breakout and adopt the Steelbreak look: mouse paddle control (optional, in Settings), a serve where the ball starts anchored on the paddle, power-ups that live inside specific 2-hit bricks instead of dropping at random, and the Steelbreak sci-fi industrial art direction replacing the Enochian one.

## Children
- T1 anchored serve (click / Space to launch)
- T2 mouse paddle control + Settings toggle
- T3 power-up bricks (2 hits, drop on break)
- T4 Steelbreak palette restyle (shapes)
- A1 Steelbreak sprite set (art pipeline)

title: Anchor the ball to the paddle and launch it on click or Space
description:
## Problem / goal
The ball currently spawns mid-screen already moving, at run start and after every lost life. The player should control the serve.

## Behaviour
- At the start of a run and after every lost life (with lives remaining), the ball sits centred on top of the paddle and moves with it (including when Super-Sizer changes the paddle width).
- While anchored, the ball does not move on its own and nothing collides with it.
- Left mouse click or Space launches it upward at `BALL_SPEED`, at 45° toward the side the paddle is currently moving (right if the paddle is still).
- Click / Space while the ball is already in flight does nothing.
- Launch input is ignored while paused.

## Out of scope
Auto-launch timer, a sticky/catch power-up, aiming the launch.

## Notes for the coder
- Add an anchored marker/state on the ball (e.g. `Anchored` component). While anchored keep it out of the simulation (zero `LinearVelocity`, or `RigidBodyDisabled` / kinematic) and snap it to the paddle each frame; gate with `run_if(in_state(PlayState::Playing))`.
- Replace the reset to (0,0) with a velocity in `ball_movement` (`src/main.rs`) and the initial `LinearVelocity` in `spawn_run_entities`.
- `ball_movement` must skip the speed renormalization / min-vertical clamp while anchored (velocity is zero).
- Tests: headless via `test_support::tap(KeyCode::Space)`; mouse via `ButtonInput<MouseButton>` (add a small helper next to `tap` if needed). `MinimalPlugins` test app may need `ButtonInput<MouseButton>` initialised.
- Space is not otherwise bound in gameplay today; P/Esc own pause.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Starting a run shows the ball resting on top of the paddle; moving the paddle carries the ball with it.
- [ ] Left-clicking launches the ball upward; pressing Space also launches it.
- [ ] After losing a life with lives remaining, the ball is anchored on the paddle again (not mid-screen).
- [ ] Clicking or pressing Space while the ball is in flight does not change its trajectory.
- [ ] While paused, click and Space do not launch the ball; after resuming it is still anchored.
- [ ] `cargo test` includes passing tests for anchored-on-start, launch-on-Space and re-anchor-after-life-lost; `trunk build` succeeds.

title: Add mouse paddle control with a Settings toggle
description:
## Problem / goal
Let the player steer the paddle with the mouse, selectable in Settings.

## Behaviour
- The Settings screen gets a "Paddle control: Mouse" / "Paddle control: Keyboard" button showing the current value; activating it (click, or Enter/Space when focused) toggles it. Default: Mouse.
- Mouse mode: the paddle follows the cursor's X position, clamped so it never enters the side walls (respecting the current paddle width).
- Arrow keys and A/D keep working in both modes. In Keyboard mode the mouse does not move the paddle.
- Session-only: the choice resets to Mouse when the app restarts.

## Out of scope
Persisting settings (config file / localStorage), mouse sensitivity, hiding or locking the cursor, gamepad.

## Notes for the coder
- New `ControlSettings` resource (e.g. `src/settings.rs` or under `src/menu/`), default `Mouse`.
- Paddle is `RigidBody::Dynamic` driven by `ConstantForce` in `paddle_movement` (`src/main.rs`). In mouse mode drive `LinearVelocity.x` toward the target X each frame (so Avian still resolves the ball bounce properly) instead of teleporting the Transform.
- Cursor -> world via `Window::cursor_position` + `Camera::viewport_to_world_2d`. Clamp with `Paddle.width` (Super-Sizer changes it) and `WINDOW_WIDTH`.
- Put target-X/clamp maths in a pure function so it is unit-testable headless (no window in tests).
- Reuse `src/menu/` (`menu_button`, focus navigation) from sim-v0i.2 / PR #8; extend `src/menu/settings.rs` (replace "Coming soon").
- Keep the paddle-hit "spin" in `ball_movement` working.
- Launch click (T1) and this both read mouse input only in `PlayState::Playing`.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Settings shows "Paddle control: Mouse" by default; activating it switches to "Keyboard" and activating again switches back.
- [ ] In Mouse mode, moving the cursor left/right makes the paddle follow it, and the paddle stops at the walls.
- [ ] In Keyboard mode, moving the mouse does not move the paddle; arrows and A/D do.
- [ ] In Mouse mode, arrows and A/D still move the paddle.
- [ ] In Mouse mode the paddle still bounces the ball, with the edge-angle spin (hitting near an edge sends the ball out at a steeper side angle).
- [ ] Works natively and in the web build (`trunk serve`); unit tests for the clamp maths pass.

title: Make power-up bricks take 2 hits and drop their power-up on break
description:
## Problem / goal
Power-ups currently drop on a timer from a random brick position. Instead, specific bricks should carry a power-up: the player targets them, they take 2 hits, and the power-up falls when the brick breaks.

## Behaviour
- Each run, exactly 6 of the 60 bricks are chosen at random to be power-up bricks. Each gets its kind from the existing weighted `PowerUpSpawner` registry.
- Power-up bricks look distinct (violet "reactor core" colour, e.g. `#b58cff`) from the start of the run.
- First hit: the brick stays, switches to a visibly cracked/darker look, +10 score.
- Second hit: the brick breaks, +10 score, and its power-up starts falling from the brick's position. Catching it with the paddle works exactly as today.
- Normal bricks still break in one hit.
- The timed random drops are removed; power-ups only ever come from broken power-up bricks.
- Win condition unchanged: the run is won when every brick (including 2-hit ones) is gone.

## Out of scope
New power-up kinds, other multi-hit brick types, level layouts, particles.

## Notes for the coder
- Components e.g. `BrickHealth(u8)` (or `Brick { hits_left }`) and `PowerUpBrick { kind }` (the kind type lives in `src/powerups/mod.rs`).
- `on_ball_collision` (`src/main.rs`) decrements health; only at 0 does it despawn and set `signals.broke_brick`. Swap the sprite colour on the cracked hit.
- Fire an event such as `BrickDestroyed { pos: Vec2, power_up: Option<PowerUpKind> }`; `src/powerups/mod.rs` observes it and spawns the falling power-up (reuse the existing spawn bundle and the per-run gravity ramp). Keeps `main.rs` ignorant of power-up internals.
- Choosing the 6 bricks: in `spawn_bricks` or via a `RestartGame`-time step owned by powerups; needs a weighted `pick()` on `Spawner<T>` (`src/spawner.rs`) without the timer. Remove the timer path from `spawn_power_ups` and update the doc comments and CLAUDE.md sections that describe timed spawns.
- Re-check the `brick_query.iter().count() <= 1` win check in `ball_movement` with 2-hit bricks (a cracked brick is still a brick).
- One ball contact must count as exactly one hit (`CollisionStart` fires once per touch start); add a test that a single bounce off a power-up brick only cracks it.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Each new run shows exactly 6 visually distinct (violet) power-up bricks, in different positions across runs.
- [ ] Hitting a power-up brick once leaves it in place with a cracked look and adds 10 points; a second hit removes it and adds 10 more.
- [ ] Breaking a power-up brick spawns a falling power-up at its position; catching it with the paddle applies the effect (Super-Sizer widens the paddle).
- [ ] No power-ups appear except from broken power-up bricks (30 s of play without breaking one produces none).
- [ ] Clearing every brick, including the 2-hit ones, still wins the run.
- [ ] `cargo test` includes passing tests for 2-hit break, drop-on-break and exactly-6-per-run.

title: Restyle the game in the Steelbreak palette (shapes)
description:
## Problem / goal
Adopt the Steelbreak sci-fi industrial look (see `art/steelbreak_concept.png`, `art/steelbreak_keyart.png`, palette in `art/gen_concept.py`) in-game now, using coloured shapes, before real sprites arrive from the art pipeline.

## Behaviour
- Background: dark hangar void `#080b0f` (ClearColor), optional panel tone `#0c1118`.
- Ball: steel grey, rendered as a circle (not a square).
- Paddle: cyan emitter `#4fd8ff`, with lighter "prongs" at each end (child shapes).
- Brick rows cycle ceramic `#ff6a4d`, titanium `#a9bacd`, tungsten `#ffab4d`.
- Power-up bricks: reactor-core violet `#b58cff`; cracked variant a darker violet.
- Falling power-ups: cyan or violet, readable against the background.
- HUD: ink `#dde6f1` values, `#8a9aab` labels, uppercase "SCORE" / "LIVES"; overlay text in the same palette.

## Out of scope
Sprites/images (art pipeline, A1), particles, scanline/vignette post effects, HUD layout redesign.

## Notes for the coder
- One `src/theme.rs` palette module holding every colour, so the later sprite swap touches one place.
- Round ball: `Mesh2d(Circle)` + `MeshMaterial2d<ColorMaterial>`; collider stays `Collider::circle`. Headless tests use `MinimalPlugins` — make sure mesh/material assets don't break `test_support::app()` (spawn may need `Assets<Mesh>` / `Assets<ColorMaterial>` guarded or initialised).
- Must not change gameplay: sizes, colliders and speeds unchanged.
- Menus from sim-v0i.2/.3 may adopt the palette too if trivial; not required.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] In-game background, ball, paddle (with end prongs), brick rows, power-up bricks (intact and cracked) and HUD use the Steelbreak colours listed in the spec; the ball renders round.
- [ ] All colours come from one `src/theme.rs` module.
- [ ] No gameplay change: all existing tests pass; the native build and `trunk build` both render the new look.

title: Concept art: Steelbreak sprite set (bricks, ball, paddle, power-up, hangar)
description:
## Subject
Steelbreak sprite set for the breakout game: sci-fi industrial hangar, steel ball, magnetic-emitter paddle, metal-plate bricks. The user chose Steelbreak over the Enochian painterly lane (2026-09-27).

## Before the first round (art-director)
- Rewrite `art/style.md` from the Enochian guide to Steelbreak: palette and material codes, brick classes and callouts from `art/steelbreak_concept.png` / `art/gen_concept.py` (hangar void `#0a0e15`, structural steel `#16202c`, polished ball `#a9bacd`, emitter field `#4fd8ff`, cold key `#a9dcff`, warm bounce `#ffab4d`, ceramic `#ff6a4d`, reactor core `#b58cff`). Move the Enoch guide to an archived file.
- `art/` is untracked in git; commit it (minus private references) with the style guide change.

## Use in game
Replaces the coloured shapes from the Steelbreak palette restyle task (T4, `src/theme.rs`).

## Asset contract
- Bricks, 4 classes: fired ceramic, titanium alloy, tungsten plate, reactor core (power-up brick). Each has intact and cracked states. Game size 80×30, author at 2×.
- Steel ball, 15 px game size (author at 4×), sphere reads as a sphere.
- Emitter paddle, 120×20 game size, horizontally stretchable (9-slice or separate prongs + field), because Super-Sizer widens it.
- Falling power-up icon, 24×24.
- Hangar background for the 900×650 play area, with a dark top-left HUD area.

## Handoff
The asset-producer files the coder issue that swaps T4's shapes for these sprites.

title: Art: Steelbreak bricks (4 classes, intact + cracked)
description:
## Subject
Four Steelbreak brick classes (fired ceramic, titanium alloy, tungsten plate, reactor core), each intact and cracked.

## Use in game
Brick entities in the 10x6 grid (`BRICK_WIDTH` 80 x `BRICK_HEIGHT` 30 in `src/main.rs`). Replaces T4's coloured rectangles (sim-rdl.4). The reactor core is the power-up brick from sim-rdl.3 (it takes 2 hits in game; its cracked state shows after the first hit).

## Variants
4 classes x 2 states = 8 sprites. Concept rounds should nail one shared plate shape/bevel; the classes differ in material and colour per the brick-class table in `art/style.md` (hand-recolouring with `artgen recolor` is fine where material reads allow). Cracked = same plate, dark fracture lines, chipped corner, same silhouette.

## Frames
None (static).

## References
`art/steelbreak_concept.png` (Brick classes panel) — usable as `--ref`. Style: `art/style.md`. No hit-count pips or text on the plate.

title: Art: Steelbreak ball, emitter paddle and power-up icon
description:
## Subject
Steel ball, magnetic-emitter paddle (stretchable) and falling power-up icon.

## Use in game
- Ball: `BALL_SIZE` 15 px circle collider.
- Paddle: `PADDLE_WIDTH` 120 x `PADDLE_HEIGHT` 20; Super-Sizer widens it by 1.25x (and more power-ups may stretch further), so it must stretch horizontally without distorting the prongs.

`art/steelbreak_concept.png` (ball + emitter paddle callouts 1 and 4). Ball reads as a sphere: hard key specular, cool cyan rim, warm amber rim. Paddle has two prongs and no solid surface between them.

title: Load sprite assets from assets/ (native + web), proven with a placeholder background
description:
## Problem / goal
The game draws only coloured shapes and has no image-asset loading, so the Steelbreak sprites (art epic sim-rdl.5) have nowhere to land. Put the loading path in place on both targets, proven with one real slot: the play-area background.

## Behaviour
- New `assets/` directory at the repo root, following the art pipeline's layout: sprites live at `assets/sprites/<name>.png`.
- A placeholder `assets/sprites/background.png` (900×650, a plain dark Steelbreak gradient `#080b0f` → `#0c1118`, committed) is drawn behind everything in the play area on the main menu and in game. sim-rdl.5.3 (hangar background) later just overwrites this file; no code change needed.
- Native (`cargo run`): the background loads from `assets/`. Editing the PNG while the game runs updates it on screen within a couple of seconds (hot reload).
- Web (`trunk build` / `trunk serve`): `assets/` is copied into `dist/` and the background renders in the browser, with no 404s in the console for `.meta` files or the PNG.
- If the file is missing, the game still runs (the dark clear colour shows) and doesn't panic.

## Out of scope
Swapping bricks, ball, paddle or power-ups to sprites (the asset-producer files a coder issue per art task), texture atlases, loading screens, the real hangar art.

## Notes for the coder
- One place for handles: a `GameSprites` resource (e.g. `src/sprites.rs`, its own `Plugin`) loaded at `Startup` through `AssetServer`. Later sprite swaps add fields there. If sim-rdl.4 has landed, sit alongside `src/theme.rs`.
- Background: `Sprite` with that handle, `custom_size` 900×650, `Transform` z well below the game (e.g. -10), global rather than `DespawnOnExit(AppState::InGame)`, so the menus show it too.
- Headless tests: `test_support::app()` runs on `MinimalPlugins` with no `AssetServer`. Register the sprites plugin from `main()` (like `ScriptPlugin`), not from `add_game`, or make it tolerate the missing asset server. `cargo test` must not need the PNG or a window.
- Web: add `<link data-trunk rel="copy-dir" href="assets" />` to `index.html`. Set `AssetPlugin { meta_check: AssetMetaCheck::Never, .. }` via `DefaultPlugins.set(...)`, otherwise Bevy requests `*.meta` files and trunk's server errors.
- Hot reload: enable bevy's `file_watcher` feature only in the non-wasm target dependencies in `Cargo.toml`, the same way `bevy_mod_scripting` is gated. The wasm build must not pull it in.
- `dist/` is being untracked by sim-ga0; don't commit build output.
- Update CLAUDE.md (module layout and the assets/wasm notes).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `assets/sprites/background.png` exists (900×650), and `cargo run` shows it behind the main menu and the game (dark gradient, not flat black).
- [ ] While `cargo run` is live, replacing `assets/sprites/background.png` with a different image updates the window within a few seconds without a restart.
- [ ] `trunk serve` shows the same background in the browser, and the devtools console/network shows no failed requests for the PNG or any `.meta` file.
- [ ] Renaming the PNG away and running `cargo run` still starts the game without a panic.
- [ ] `cargo tree --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -e features` shows no `file_watcher` feature on bevy (it is native-only).
- [ ] `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `trunk build` pass.

title: Replace GameStatus with Bevy States and pause physics outside play
description:
## Problem / goal
Replace the hand-checked `GameStatus` resource with a real Bevy state machine as the foundation for menus. No new UI in this task.

## Behaviour
- `AppState { MainMenu, InGame, GameOver }` plus an `InGame` sub-state `PlayState { Playing, Paused }`. In this task the initial state is `InGame` (the menu arrives in the next task).
- Ball, paddle, bricks and HUD spawn when entering `InGame` and are removed when leaving it. Walls and camera stay global.
- Avian's physics clock (`Time<Physics>`) is paused whenever the state is not `InGame/Playing`, and resumed when it is. This replaces the manual velocity-zeroing at game end.
- P or Esc toggles Playing <-> Paused; the existing overlay text shows while paused.
- Losing the last life or clearing all bricks goes to `GameOver`, with a won/lost outcome kept in a resource; the existing text is shown; R starts a new run.
- A new run always resets score to 0 and lives to 3 (one constant); the lives label is driven by that constant. `RestartGame` is still broadcast so power-ups reset themselves.
- Remove the unused `QuitGamme` event.

## Out of scope
Any new menu UI (next tasks), settings, audio.

## Notes for the coder
- `GameStatus` checks to replace: `src/main.rs` (`paddle_movement`, `on_ball_collision`, `ball_movement`, `restart_game`, `update_ui`) and `src/powerups/mod.rs` (3 systems, ~lines 103/143/162). Prefer `run_if(in_state(...))`.
- Keep the `PaddleMovementSet` / `TickActiveEffects` ordering sets working.
- The `RestartGame` observer pattern (`reset_on_restart`) must still fire on every new run.
- Power-up timers must not tick while paused: check what clock `ActiveEffects` ticks on, or gate the tick system.
- Lives today: initial 5 (`insert_resource(Lives(5))`), restart 3, label hard-coded "Lives: 3" — unify on 3.
- Must still build for wasm; don't touch the scripting cfg-gates. Update CLAUDE.md's `GameStatus` notes to describe the state machine.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] `cargo build` and `trunk build` both succeed.
- [ ] On launch, the game plays as it does today (ball moves, paddle responds, bricks break, score goes up).
- [ ] Pressing P or Esc while playing freezes the ball, paddle, falling power-ups and active power-up timers and shows the paused text; pressing P or Esc again resumes from the same positions.
- [ ] Losing all lives shows the game-over text and nothing on screen keeps moving.
- [ ] Clearing all bricks shows the win text and nothing on screen keeps moving.
- [ ] Pressing R on the game-over/win screen starts a fresh run: score 0, lives 3, full brick wall, no active power-ups.
- [ ] The HUD shows "Lives: 3" on first launch and after every restart.
close_reason: Bevy States repllace GameStatus; physics paused outside play (PR #7)

title: Add main menu and Settings screen
description:
## Problem / goal
Give the game a title/main menu so the player chooses to start, with a Settings entry that later work will fill in.

## Behaviour
- The app starts in `MainMenu`: title "BREAKOUT" and buttons **Start**, **Settings**, **Quit** (Quit native only; not spawned on wasm). The game world is not visible or simulating behind the menu.
- Start -> `InGame/Playing` with a fresh run (score 0, lives 3).
- Settings -> new `AppState::Settings` screen: heading "Settings", text "Coming soon", a **Back** button returning to the main menu. Esc on Settings also goes back.
- Quit -> exits the app.
- Input: buttons show hover and pressed states under the mouse and respond to clicks. Up/Down or W/S moves a visible focus highlight (wrapping), Enter or Space activates the focused button.
- Button, focus and navigation code lives in a small reusable module `src/menu/` that the pause / game-over task reuses.

## Out of scope
Actual settings, pause menu and game-over screen (next task), gamepad, transitions.

## Notes for the coder
- Bevy UI (`Node`, `Button`, `Interaction`), with screen entities scoped to their state (despawned on exit).
- Quit: `#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]`, write `AppExit`.
- Builds on the AppState from the previous task; change the initial state to `MainMenu`.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Launching (native and web) shows the main menu with Start and Settings, plus Quit on native only; no ball moves behind it.
- [x] Clicking Start begins a game with score 0 and lives 3.
- [x] Clicking Settings shows "Settings" / "Coming soon" with a Back button; clicking Back or pressing Esc returns to the main menu.
- [x] Up/Down (or W/S) visibly moves the highlight between buttons and wraps around; Enter or Space activates the highlighted button.
- [x] Hovering a button with the mouse changes its appearance.
- [x] On native, Quit closes the window; the browser build shows no Quit button.
- [x] `cargo build` and `trunk build` succeed.

title: Add pause menu and Game Over / Win screen
description:
## Problem / goal
Turn the text-only pause and end-of-game overlays into real menus so the player can resume, replay, or return to the title screen.

## Behaviour
- Paused: a menu over the frozen game with title "Paused" and buttons **Resume** and **Main menu**. P or Esc still toggles pause. Main menu abandons the run.
- GameOver: shows "GAME OVER" or "YOU WIN!", the final score, and buttons **Play again** and **Main menu**. R still works as a Play again shortcut.
- Both screens reuse the `src/menu/` module (same mouse + keyboard behaviour as the main menu).

## Out of scope
Restart-from-pause, high scores, transitions/animations.

## Notes for the coder
- Replaces the `GameOverText` overlay strings in `update_ui`.
- Main menu -> MainMenu must fully tear down the run so Start begins fresh (RestartGame still reaches power-ups).
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Pressing Esc or P mid-game shows a Paused menu with Resume and Main menu; the game behind it is frozen.
- [x] Resume (click, Enter, or Esc/P) continues the game exactly where it was.
- [x] Main menu from pause returns to the title menu; Start from there begins a fresh run (score 0, lives 3, full bricks, no power-ups).
- [ ] Losing shows "GAME OVER" with the final score; winning shows "YOU WIN!" with the final score.
- [ ] Play again (click, Enter, or R) starts a fresh run; Main menu returns to the title screen.
- [x] `cargo build` and `trunk build` succeed.
